name: SX1509 16-I/O expander breakout
description: Semtech 16-channel I2C GPIO expander with level shifting, LED driver (PWM/blink/breathe) and keypad engine: two 8-bit banks (IO0-7 on VCC1, IO8-15 on VCC2), each pin an input (5.5 V tolerant, pull-up/down) or an output (8 mA source, 15 mA sink). Runs on 1.425-3.6 V (not 5 V). Sold as: SparkFun 16 Output I/O Expander Breakout - SX1509 (BOB-13601; top header INT RST GND 3V3 SDA SCL, bottom header OSC RST GND 3.3V SDA SCL, I/O columns GND 0-3 VCC1 4-7 and 8-11 VCC2 12-15 GND; 10k pull-ups on SDA, SCL, RST and INT), I2C address 0x3E (0x3F/0x70/0x71 via the ADD jumpers).
eli5: Gives your board 16 extra pins to light LEDs or read buttons, using only the two I2C wires.

supplierQuery: SparkFun SX1509 16 output I/O expander breakout BOB-13601
buildNotes: Power it from 3.3 V only: the SX1509's supply is 1.425-3.6 V (absolute max 3.7 V). Its I/O pins tolerate 5.5 V as inputs.
I2C address is 0x3E with both ADD jumpers on the back at 0; 0x3F, 0x70 and 0x71 by re-soldering ADD0/ADD1.
Register pairs are Bank B (IO8-15) first, then Bank A (IO0-7): RegDirB 0x0E / RegDirA 0x0F (1 = input, reset 0xFF), RegDataB 0x10 / RegDataA 0x11, RegPullUpB 0x06 / RegPullUpA 0x07.
RegData is written to set outputs and read to get pin levels. All pins power up as inputs with the data latches high, so write the latch low before switching a pin to output if it must start off.
Software reset: write 0x12 then 0x34 to RegReset (0x7D).
Each I/O sources up to 8 mA and sinks up to 15 mA (VCCx >= 2 V): always put a resistor in series with an LED. Sinking (LED from 3.3 V to the pin) gives more current.
The outer rail next to each I/O column is GND by default (rear jumpers can move it to VCC1/VCC2). Don't solder both rows of headers if you want to use a breadboard.
RST, INT and OSC are optional; RST and INT already have 10k pull-ups.

driver.code:
# SX1509 16-channel I2C GPIO expander (Semtech SX1509, datasheet rev 1), MicroPython driver.
# SX1509 register map (section 5.3). Every pair is Bank B (IO8-IO15) FIRST, then Bank A (IO0-IO7):
#   RegInputDisableB/A 0x00/0x01  1 = input buffer off (reset 0x00)
#   RegPullUpB/A       0x06/0x07  1 = internal pull-up on
#   RegPullDownB/A     0x08/0x09  1 = internal pull-down on
#   RegOpenDrainB/A    0x0A/0x0B  1 = open-drain output
#   RegDirB/A          0x0E/0x0F  1 = input (reset 0xFF), 0 = output
#   RegDataB/A         0x10/0x11  write = output level, read = level seen at the pins (reset 0xFF)
#   RegInterruptMaskA  0x13       reset 0xFF (used as a presence check)
#   RegReset           0x7D       write 0x12 then 0x34 = software reset to defaults
# Address: 0x3E (ADDR1 ADDR0 = 00), 0x3F (01), 0x70 (10), 0x71 (11).
# Pins are numbered 0-15 as printed on the board: 0-7 = Bank A, 8-15 = Bank B.

_INPUT_DISABLE_B = 0x00
_PULLUP_B = 0x06
_PULLDOWN_B = 0x08
_OPEN_DRAIN_B = 0x0A
_DIR_B = 0x0E
_DATA_B = 0x10
_INT_MASK_A = 0x13
_RESET = 0x7D

INPUT = 1
OUTPUT = 0


class SX1509:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x3E, reset=True):
        """addr 0x3E with both ADD jumpers at 0 (SparkFun BOB-13601 default)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if reset:
            # Software reset (datasheet 4.4.2): 0x12 then 0x34 to RegReset.
            self._w(_RESET, 0x12)
            self._w(_RESET, 0x34)
        # RegInterruptMaskA resets to 0xFF: a quick check that an SX1509 answers.
        if self._r(_INT_MASK_A) != 0xFF:
            raise OSError('SX1509 not found at 0x%02X' % addr)
        # Shadow of the output latches (RegData resets to 0xFFFF). Reading RegData returns
        # pin levels, not the latch, so outputs are changed from this copy.
        self._out = 0xFFFF

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _r16(self, reg_b):
        """Read a Bank B / Bank A register pair as a 16-bit value (bits 0-7 = IO0-7)."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg_b, 2)  # B then A (auto-increment)
        return d[1] | (d[0] << 8)

    def _w16(self, reg_b, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg_b, bytes([(val >> 8) & 0xFF, val & 0xFF]))

    def _bit(self, reg_b, pin, on):
        if not 0 <= pin <= 15:
            raise ValueError('pin must be 0-15')
        reg = reg_b if pin >= 8 else reg_b + 1  # Bank B register, or Bank A right after it
        v = self._r(reg)
        m = 1 << (pin & 7)
        self._w(reg, (v | m) if on else (v & ~m))

    def pin_mode(self, pin, mode, pull=None):
        """mode INPUT or OUTPUT; pull = 'up', 'down' or None (inputs only)."""
        if mode == OUTPUT:
            self._bit(_PULLUP_B, pin, False)
            self._bit(_PULLDOWN_B, pin, False)
            self._bit(_OPEN_DRAIN_B, pin, False)
            self._bit(_DIR_B, pin, False)
        else:
            self._bit(_INPUT_DISABLE_B, pin, False)
            self._bit(_PULLUP_B, pin, pull == 'up')
            self._bit(_PULLDOWN_B, pin, pull == 'down')
            self._bit(_DIR_B, pin, True)

    def value(self, pin, val=None):
        """Read the level at a pin (RegData read), or set an output pin's level."""
        if not 0 <= pin <= 15:
            raise ValueError('pin must be 0-15')
        if val is None:
            reg = _DATA_B if pin >= 8 else _DATA_B + 1
            return (self._r(reg) >> (pin & 7)) & 1
        if val:
            self._out |= 1 << pin
        else:
            self._out &= ~(1 << pin)
        reg = _DATA_B if pin >= 8 else _DATA_B + 1
        self._w(reg, (self._out >> (8 if pin >= 8 else 0)) & 0xFF)

    def read_port(self):
        """All 16 pin levels: bits 0-7 = IO0-7, bits 8-15 = IO8-15."""
        return self._r16(_DATA_B)

    def write_port(self, val):
        """Set all 16 output levels (only output-configured pins drive them)."""
        self._out = val & 0xFFFF
        self._w16(_DATA_B, self._out)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sx1509 import SX1509, INPUT, OUTPUT

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
io = SX1509(i2c)                   # address 0x3E (ADD jumpers at 0)
io.value(0, 0)                     # IO0 latch low before it becomes an output
io.pin_mode(0, OUTPUT)             # IO0 drives an LED (through a resistor)
io.pin_mode(8, INPUT, pull='up')   # IO8 reads a button wired to GND
while True:
    pressed = 1 if io.value(8) == 0 else 0
    io.value(0, pressed)           # LED on while the button is held
    print('BTN=%d LED=%d' % (pressed, pressed))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
